mediaRemoteAdapter.note: Built as an embedded, unlinked arm64 framework by project.yml. The bundled Perl entry point reads system now-playing metadata only while a wallpaper has media integration enabled. Its `send` command is now invoked as well, but only for the three transport actions a user can bind to a wallpaper's own `usershortcut` property (TogglePlayPause, NextTrack, PreviousTrack), only for a wallpaper listed by system_media_scene_handles, and only as a short-lived process off the main actor. A wallpaper cannot name a command: it names one of its own properties, and the value its user chose decides what happens. The test client is not invoked.

sceneEngine.equalQualityPerformanceChanges: 2026-09-24: Metal and Vulkan borrow their synchronous per-pass uniform writer through std::cref without changing UpdateUniformOp. ShaderValue packs MatrixBase coefficients column-major into its existing owning inline/vector storage; non-direct expressions evaluate once in the original scalar type. AudioResponseService uses a shared logical FIFO read offset and bounded append-time compaction/geometric capacity growth while retaining the 1024-frame FFT window, 200-frame hop and 24000-frame limit. Matrix ownership/layout and continuous stereo-window regressions cover the changes; oversized comparisons wait for all 115 windows. Upstream revisions are unchanged.
sceneEngine.note: 2026-09-24 (texture decode at pass preparation): CustomShaderPass::prepare asks TextureCache::FindTex before parsing a package or loose image, because CreateTex answers a cached key without reading the pixels it is handed; a texture bound by several passes is no longer decoded once per pass. Runtime images keep resolving through the parser. New TexturePrefetch (Scene/VulkanRender) decodes the images the unprepared passes will parse on up to six worker threads, ahead of the pass that binds them; RenderingResources::texture_prefetch carries it only while VulkanRender::preparePasses runs, and offscreen_scene_probe drives preparation the same way. Uploads, their order and the texture cache stay on the preparing thread. Decoding and untaken images are held under a 256 MiB budget estimated from each header (RGBA8 plus a mip chain; one larger image is admitted alone) and admitted strictly in request order; preparation never waits on an image not yet admitted and decodes that one itself. Videos, sprite sheets, runtime images, render targets and uploaded textures are not prefetched. A 943 MB puppet scene of 122 embedded PNG textures (1264 Mpx) reached its first offscreen frame in 15.6 s, dominated by single-threaded stb_image inflate; 14.7 s with the FindTex check alone and 3.6 s with the prefetch, with a byte-identical frame and peak RSS rising from about 0.8 to 1.1 GB. A worker thread that fails to start is dropped rather than unwinding with joinable threads; with none, preparation decodes every image itself. texture_prefetch_test covers ordering, the budget, admission skipping, a pool that could not start, decode failures and teardown. Upstream revisions are unchanged. 2026-09-24 (interleaved feedback-copy correctness): MetalRender retains pending opening copies by destination texture instead of one copy_into/copy_from slot, so copy A to Ac and copy B to Bc can both remain pending until B then A renders. The per-frame storage is cleared on frame abandonment and graph release. InterleavedFeedbackCopiesPreserveEachReadersImage compares both targets against the ordinary blit path over four frames; restoring single-slot overwrite semantics corrupts A and fails the pixel check. No frame-clock scheduling code changed. 2026-09-24 (Metal render passes, uniform lookups and reuse sampling): MetalRender::drawFrame keeps one render command encoder open across consecutive passes into the same target texture, the rule PlanCustomPassBatches batches the compatibility backend by. A pass starts a new render pass only for another target, another depth attachment, a read of its own target (resolved through the target table, so copy-plan aliases count), or a clear, unless the open render pass began with that same clear and has drawn nothing; a draw that shares a render pass sets the pipeline, the depth-stencil state and every texture and sampler slot it declares, nil included, so nothing the previous draw bound leaks into it. A pass whose layer is hidden (passDraws false, the predicate the old hidden-pass check used) writes no uniforms, uploads no dynamic mesh and opens no encoder unless it carries a clear, as CustomShaderPass::updateFrame does. Per-pass colour and depth textures are resolved once per target-table change (refreshPassTargets, from compile and applySceneOptimizationSetting). writeUniforms resolves reflection members by write position (UniformWriteSlot on PreparedPass and VideoPlaneDraw), comparing names instead of hashing each one into the reflection every frame. StaticSubgraphCache::PassSampled names the passes Plan reads; both backends take no frameSample for the rest, and Metal, like Vulkan already, stops planning while nothing is pinned. Test-only MetalRender::LastFrameEncodeCountsForTests reports render passes, scene-output render passes and blits per frame; metal_scene_draw_smoke prints them with thread CPU per drawFrame for WE_TEST_METAL_PROJECTS and adds LayersSharingATargetShareOneRenderPassAndHiddenLayersCostNone, and static_subgraph_cache_test adds OnlyWritersOfCacheableTargetsAreSampled. Workshop 3620484312 at 3456x2234: 179 to 47 render passes per frame (154 to 22 into the scene's own image; the other 21 each follow a full-frame copy of that image a clipping-mask effect reads), 1.82 to 0.75 ms CPU per drawFrame, byte-identical output. 2026-09-24 (Metal feedback copies): a copy the graph inserts only so the next pass can sample the image it draws into (a material reading _rt_FullFrameBuffer) is replaced by trading the two names' textures. planFeedbackSwaps plans it, after the reuse table, only where exact: both textures private to one name, equal size, RGBA8Unorm, one mip level, no depth attachment on either name, neither target cacheable, and the reader the next pass to touch the source, drawing into it without reading it and loading it (a clearing reader needs no opening copy). At encode time the copy's name takes the source texture, the source's name the copy's texture, and the reader's render pass opens with DontCare and a full-target draw of owe_copy_fragment, which reads the old image texel for texel; a reader that does not render that frame gets the copy as a blit instead, and an abandoned frame undoes its trades. Gated with the rest of the copy plan by scene optimisation; WALLPAPER_MACHINE_FEEDBACK_COPIES=1 forces the copies for A/B measurement. metal_scene_draw_smoke adds AFeedbackCopyTradesTexturesAndDrawsTheSamePicture. Workshop 3620484312: 21 to 0 blits per frame, 47 render passes unchanged, byte-identical output. 2026-09-23 (camera parallax for nested layers): WPShaderValueUpdater offsets a layer by its scene position (the translation of the matrix it is drawn with) instead of its parent-relative origin. A layer inside a group has a local origin near zero, so a full-screen child of a centred group was pushed as if it sat in the canvas corner: in Workshop 3632513108 the intro layer moved 69 x 39 px, beyond its 1.02 overscan, and uncovered the layers beneath it along the left and bottom edges. Top-level layers are unchanged (local and scene origin agree); effect final nodes now follow the same rule; both renderers share this updater. Regression: ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.CameraParallaxPlacesAChildLayerByItsScenePosition in script_runtime_compat_test. 2026-09-22 (scenetexture slots, camera-object zoom, layer parents and alpha): a `usertextures` entry that names one of the wallpaper's own `scenetexture` properties now takes that property's value. Tests: metal_backend_test.cpp, metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm and static_subgraph_cache_test.cpp extended. 2026-09-19 (round 10): direct NV12 plane sampling, and scene optimisation applied at a frame boundary. WPSceneParser records each pending translation's texture keys and, for a material with exactly one video slot the native video path accepts, compiles a second program from copies of the same units and shader info; SceneMetalProgram gains SceneMetalVideoPlaneVariant, whose failure is recorded on the variant and never on the program. WPShaderParser::CompileToMslRust takes an optional plane slot and RustShaderBridge writes video_planes only when set. MetalVideoTextures asks each key's consumers what they need before importing: a frame every consumer samples as planes encodes no conversion and acquires no destination, a mixed scene converts once, the path is decided from the frame's real pixel format every frame, a demand change re-imports the current generation rather than waiting, and the bundle a frame is sampled from is retained into every command buffer that reads it rather than only the one that imported it. MetalRender builds both programs' binding plans through one shared BuildMetalResourcePlan, builds both pipelines with the graph, reserves the larger uniform block, writes the colour constants from the decoded frame, and binds the luma plane with the author's sampler and the chroma plane with a linear-filtered copy of it. MetalVideoSupport owns the process-wide switch (default off) and Scene/include/Scene/SceneVideoPath.hpp the reported path. Scene optimisation: MetalRender::applySceneOptimizationSetting and VulkanRender::ApplySceneOptimization rebuild the copy plan, the targets it governs and the reuse table over the graph already compiled, called from SceneWallpaper's frame loop; compileStaticCache now gives its pinned bytes back before recounting them, compile() builds a present pipeline for every copy target so an un-elided copy never compiles inside a frame, and the Vulkan path quiesces before destroying prepared pass state exactly as applyRenderScale does. Tests: metal_video_texture_test.mm, metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm (a parsed author material over real decoded media) and crates/shader/tests/video_planes.rs. 2026-09-19 (round 11): text layers and runtime-replaced images reach the native Metal backend, and the optional plane-sampling program leaves the load path. MetalRender builds the variant's library and pipeline on a serial queue, adopts the result at a frame boundary through a generation-tagged mailbox owned by a shared pointer, and gives the variant its own uniform ring. MetalPipelineKey::program_id becomes a content hash instead of the program's address, and the library and pipeline caches move into one process-wide MetalProgramCache scoped by MTLDevice.registryID and bounded. Tests: metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm (text end to end, unchanged-text dedup, program reuse across renderers, and the video cases rewritten around the background preparation). 2026-09-19 (round 12): whole-scene idling is separated from resource mutability. SceneMesh carries MeshUpdate (Fixed/PerFrame/OnEvent) instead of a bool -- Dynamic() is unchanged for every upload and reuse decision -- text cards are OnEvent and particle meshes PerFrame; CustomShaderPass and MetalRender raise the new DynamicReason::EventMesh, StaticSubgraphCache treats it exactly like DynamicMesh for cacheability, and SceneDemandMapping deliberately does not carry it to the scene level. SceneWallpaper installs that handler through a shared target cleared in the render handler's destructor, and delivers the scene's shader-cache path with the SET_SCENE message. WPShaderParser::CompileMslVariant takes that cache root and mounts only /cache, so an optional variant's MSL, reflection and binding metadata are restored from the existing programs01 store across launches; program-cache entries are now published atomically through the new fs::Fs::Rename (implemented by PhysicalFs, refused across mounts by VFS). MetalProgramCache keeps an MTLBinaryArchive per (device, cache directory) -- the path is set on the surface's own MetalRender with its scene, so two displays showing different wallpapers do not file over each other -- attaches it to production pipeline descriptors, collects misses and serialises them on a serial queue with a debounced atomic publish, and never uses MTLPipelineOptionFailOnBinaryArchiveMiss outside a test. SceneIndexArray gains SceneIndexWidth, DrawIndexCount/DrawIndexBytes and a (quadCount, width) constructor; WPParticleRawGener writes uint32 indices when the mesh says so. MetalRender and CustomShaderPass bind MTLIndexTypeUInt32 / VK_INDEX_TYPE_UINT32 from that width. Tests: scene_mesh_tests capacity math, particle_rope_geometry_test index width and order, metal_scene_draw_smoke ARopeTrailPastTheOldSixteenBitIndexLimitStaysARopeTrail. 2026-09-19 (round 14 item 3): rope/rope-trail UV scale is encoded in the trail-length the generator writes (no author uniform). uvscrolling measures V against mesh/history capacity so a growing rope unrolls instead of stretching. uvsmoothing eases trail-position with smoothstep. Runtime updates go through ParticleSubSystem::SetRopeUv and ParticleRenderScale without re-parsing. 2026-09-19 (round 14 item 2): Native Metal accepts perspective cameras for the layer types it already draws. The whole-scene IsPerspective refusals are gone; projection is SceneCamera's FOV/aspect/near/far through the existing Metal clip-space fold; depth attachments are allocated only for passes whose material depth-tests, at the colour target's size; g_Orientation* follows the camera node; perspective hit tests unproject onto the layer plane. Tests in metal_backend_test and MetalSceneDraw.APerspectiveCameraDrawsThroughTheAuthoredShader. Also 2026-09-19 (round 14 item 1): layer-as-texture. Authored `_rt_imageLayerComposite_<id>[_a|_b]` is resolved in two phases onto `_rt_link_<id>` with explicit missing/duplicate/cycle/history reasons; hidden sources still produce an isolated composite. Both backends consume that description. 2026-09-20 (round 14 empty-key follow-up): MetalRender BuildMetalResourcePlan leaves unsampled in-range texture/sampler slots and an unused GlobalUniforms buffer unbound, matching Vulkan CustomShaderPass empty-name skip / SPIR-V omitted descriptors. prepareDraw missing-image message names slot and shader. 2026-09-19: the build pins the FFmpeg headers pkg-config resolved ahead of every other include directory (wescene_prefer_ffmpeg_headers in CMakeLists.txt, applied to wescene-renderer, wpAudio and the FFmpeg-linking tests) because a second Homebrew FFmpeg linked into /opt/homebrew/include was reaching the compiler first and its AVFrame layout left best_effort_timestamp reading a neighbouring field, which stamped every decoded frame at time zero and froze scene video textures; src/Video/FfmpegAbi.hpp refuses to decode or probe when the loaded libav* majors are not the compiled ones, and a decode thread that dies now logs why instead of leaving the last frame on screen in silence.
